title: Care Team Training Questions: Late Factory-Capacity Notices and Guarantee Weeks — Factory Production Orders
content:
**Rule taught.** For Factory Production Orders, late-notice weeks are added to the on-time guarantee by when the most recent factory-capacity delay notice was recorded:

- recorded **after the committed ship date** — adds **2 weeks**;
- recorded **on one of the three calendar days before the committed ship date, or on it** — adds **1 week**;
- recorded earlier, or never — adds none.

Late-notice weeks are added to the full weeks late to make up the credited weeks, and they count only when at least one full week late results.

## Questions and answers

**Which notice is compared?** Only the most recent delay notice with cause factory capacity on the order's milestone records, by the date it was recorded. Earlier factory-capacity notices, and notices of other causes, play no part here.

**Which date is it compared with?** The committed ship date printed on the acknowledgment, from the factory order record — not the current ship date.

**What if the order shipped within the grace period?** No full week late results, so no late-notice weeks are added either.

## Boundary table (hypothetical committed ship date: 10 June)

| Most recent factory-capacity notice recorded | Weeks added |
|---|---|
| 11 June | 2 |
| 10 June | 1 |
| 7 June | 1 |
| 6 June | none |
| no factory-capacity notice | none |

## Worked case (hypothetical)

An order shipped 1 full week late; its most recent factory-capacity notice was recorded two days after the committed ship date. The credited weeks are 1 full week late and 2 late-notice weeks, 3 in all.
